note: Curated waypoint descriptions, keyed by the stable ids in data/waypoint-ids.json. Applied by scripts/build-trails.ts (overriding any description from the GPX source) and uploadable to the comments API with scripts/upload-descriptions.ts. Listed in walking order from Denmans Cove to Fortescue Bay, with the off-route waypoints (the Cape Pillar spur and Bare Knoll) appended at the end. Pillars of the south, Monument Lookout and Seal spa have no entry: no Parks and Wildlife Service Tasmania page names them. Temporary closures are dated ('As of October 2026') so they can be found and removed. Sources for each fact: plans/waypoint-description-sources.md.

descriptions.name: Denmans Cove
descriptions.description: The start of the Three Capes Track, a bay reached only on the walkers' boat from the Port Arthur Historic Site, a trip of up to 75 minutes. A creek flows out over the beach and the sandbanks move about, so the landing can be a short wade; from September to December the water is knee-deep at times. As of October 2026 PWS Tasmania lists the track's next annual maintenance closure as 5–18 April 2027.

descriptions.name: Surveyors Cabin
descriptions.description: The first night's cabin, about 4 km from Denmans Cove through eucalypt woodland and coastal heath, its deck facing Cape Raoul. As at all three cabins, the beds are for booked Three Capes walkers only: shared bunk rooms for 48, a heated dining hub with gas cooktops, toilets, and untreated rainwater from tanks. There is mobile reception.

descriptions.name: Arthurs Peak
descriptions.description: A short climb on the second day to a summit of about 300 m, looking over Crescent Bay to Cape Raoul. Past it the track comes down off the wooded flanks of Crescent Mountain and crosses the Ellarwey Valley, wide and exposed to the wind.

descriptions.name: Retakunna Cabin
descriptions.description: The third night's cabin, near Retakunna Creek among forest and heath, looking towards Mount Fortescue. Booked walkers only, with the same shared bunk rooms, heated dining hub, gas cooktops, toilets and untreated tank water as the other two cabins. There is mobile reception.

descriptions.name: Mount Fortescue
descriptions.description: The track's last climb, on the fourth morning, through wet forest to a summit of about 490 m. After it the track runs out to Cape Hauy, and from there the walk to Fortescue Bay is mainly downhill.

descriptions.name: Mill Creek Campsite
descriptions.description: One of Fortescue Bay's two campgrounds, with bigger sites for boats, campervans and motorhomes; generators may run until 9 pm. The tank water is untreated. Camping fees apply, and sites must be booked from October to April.

descriptions.name: Fortescue Bay Campground
descriptions.description: The end of the track, on a broad white beach edged by tall stringybark forest. The campground has toilets, token-operated showers at Banksia, untreated tank water and a site office selling ice and basic camping gear; the closest groceries are at Nubeena, 45 minutes' drive away. The walkers' bus back to Port Arthur takes 30 minutes.

descriptions.name: Bare Knoll Campground
descriptions.description: Campground for independent walkers on the Cape Pillar Track, about 1 km past the crossroads with the Old Cape Pillar Track, with 12 tent platforms and a toilet. There is no reliable natural water. Stays are registered at the Fortescue Bay site office, and the Three Capes cabins are open only to Three Capes walkers. As of October 2026 PWS Tasmania lists 5–18 April 2027 as the next annual closure.

descriptions.name: Munro Cabin
descriptions.description: The second night's cabin, looking across Munro Bight to Cape Hauy. It is the only cabin with showers (two, outdoors), and mobile reception here is limited. Booked walkers only; the third day's walk to Cape Pillar leaves from and returns to Munro, so packs stay at the cabin.

descriptions.name: Drinking water
descriptions.description: Rainwater tank at Munro Cabin. The tanks at the three cabins are the only water Parks and Wildlife Service Tasmania lists along the track, and the water is untreated.

descriptions.name: The Blade
descriptions.description: High point at Cape Pillar, at the far end of the third day's out-and-back from Munro, looking across the water to Tasman Island.
